transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-12-07
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~58m
Attendees: Jenna Park (Redwood AE), Marco Alvarez (Redwood SE), Elena Martinez (Horizon - Head of Infosec), Tom Brooks (Horizon CTO), Priya Singh (Horizon Eng Mgmt)

Summary/Context (auto):
Horizon Ventures evaluating Redwood for inference layer for customer-facing features. Primary blockers: strict EU/US data residency requirements, KMS custody and BYOK needs, and subprocessor onboarding timelines for procurement. Horizon requests evidence and an architectural deep dive to validate no cross-border processing for EU data.

[00:00] Jenna: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Quick roll call - I'm Jenna Park from Redwood, AE, and Marco is our SE. Over to you horizon folks for intros?
[00:12] Elena: Hi all, Elena here, Head of Infosec at Horizon. We're primarily worried about where data is processed, and who holds keys. We have customers in the EU so we need strict region pinning and proof that nothing leaves EU.
[00:26] Tom: Tom, CTO. We'll also want to know about latency tradeoffs between dedicated capacity and a private VPC option.
[00:34] Priya: Priya, engineering. I'll own the integration work if we go forward.
[00:39] Marco: Quick agenda - we'll cover region partitioning, KMS options (BYOK, Redwood-managed, escrow), subprocessor map, and audit logs/SSO. Save questions as we go.
[00:52] Elena: Sounds good. Can you start with region pinning? How do you ensure EU data stays in EU region?
[01:00] Marco: Sure. For hosted we have region affinity options where requests are routed to EU clusters. For Dedicated and Private you can pin services to specific regions or run the private control plane in your VPC so keys and control never leave your network. In practice we do a region routing policy and have per-customer tenancy for dedicated pools.
[01:22] Elena: When you say "private control plane" is that fully customer-managed or is there still a Redwood piece that could cause cross-border telemetry?
[01:30] Marco: Good question. Our Private deployment can be deployed with a customer-managed control plane; telemetry and audit logs can be retained on-prem. The managed option keeps metrics to a minimal heartbeat back to Redwood for billing and support, but that can be disabled per contract. Note: there are sometimes log shippers that we can configure to avoid cross-border exports.
[01:52] Tom: And for hosted, is there any scenario where EU requests land on US infra for fallback? e.g. during capacity bursts?
[02:00] Marco: We have fallback policies. By default regional affinity prevents cross-border routing, but for some tiers we can enable multi-region fallbacks. For EU-only compliance you can require strict region pinning and block fallback. That may affect latency if EU capacity is saturated.
[02:22] Elena: Do you have a formal SLA or written guarantee on no cross-border processing? We need contractual language for procurement.
[02:30] Jenna: We can provide region affinity commitments in the DPA and add escrow language for keys. We'll follow up with contract language.
[02:40] Priya: OK. Next KMS - what's supported? BYOK? HSM? KMS escrow?
[02:47] Marco: We support three models: Redwood-managed keys (default), Customer-managed KMS (bring your own key, BYOK) integrated via Cloud KMS (GCP KMS, AWS KMS, Azure Key Vault), and a key escrow option for long-term audits where keys are held in an HSM escrow controlled by a neutral third party. Each has tradeoffs.
[03:12] Elena: For BYOK, where do the keys live? Are they ever copied to Redwood servers?
[03:18] Marco: With BYOK we use envelope encryption. The customer key in their KMS wraps a data key; the wrapped key is stored, but the unwrapped plaintext key is never exported. The runtime will request unwrap operations via KMS in-region. There are cached plaintext keys in memory in the runtime for a short TTL (we call that the token cache).
[03:40] Elena: That token cache — how long, and is that subject to SA access?
[03:44] Marco: The in-memory cache TTL is configurable, default 300s. Access is limited by RBAC; our operators do not have access to runtime memory. We have controls and audit logs to show key access events. The transcript may show KV cache but that's a different layer - sorry if that term got weird in docs (sometimes transcribed as KV cash).
[04:06] Tom: Escrow - who is the escrow provider? Is it an HSM backed vendor?
[04:11] Marco: We work with multiple neutral escrow providers and HSM vendors; we can propose vendors in the architecture doc. Escrow keys are stored in an HSM; access requires multi-party approval and we can include audit trails for any unwrapping.
[04:28] Elena: Will the escrow option still keep processing inside EU? The escrow partner may be outside EU which is a problem for us.
[04:35] Marco: Good callout. We can choose an escrow partner with EU residency. We'll flag that in the vendor list we send. It's a selection item for procurement.
[04:46] Priya: From integration perspective, what changes for us if we use BYOK vs Redwood-managed? More code?
[04:52] Marco: Minimal. BYOK requires KMS permissions and a short integration to do unwrap calls during runtime startup. We provide a client library and a sample VPC diagram. The heavy lifting is in provisioning the KMS key and granting permissions. We'll include sample Terraform snippets.
[05:12] Elena: Audit logs - retention and tamper protection? We need at least 7 years of retention for certain data and tamper-proof evidence for auditors.
[05:20] Marco: Logs are write-once to an append-only store; we can configure retention windows up to multi-year with export to your S3 or your on-prem object store. For tamper evidence we support immutable log exports and signed log blobs. We'll provide a log retention and export playbook.
[05:40] Tom: SSO and RBAC - how are developers provisioned and how are roles scoped?
[05:45] Jenna: We tie into SAML/SSO providers for provisioning. RBAC supports fine-grained roles (admin, operator, reader, model-deployer). We can map SAML groups to roles and provide audit trails for role changes.
[05:59] Elena: Any SOC 2 evidence for key management controls? We need proof of policies and tested controls.
[06:04] Jenna: We'll share the SOC 2 Type II report and sections that cover key management and access controls. We'll redact IP but include control narratives.
[06:12] Elena: Great. Also need ISO 27001 artifacts?
[06:15] Jenna: We have a roadmap for ISO; current status is in-progress. We can give ISO scope documents, but full certification may be later. We'll be explicit in the doc.
[06:25] Tom: Procurement will want a subprocessor matrix with contact points and data flow diagrams.
[06:30] Marco: We'll export our subprocessors and include regions where they operate and the purpose. We'll annotate which subprocessors touch PII or tokens vs non-sensitive meta data.
[06:42] Priya: Can you show an example of a cross-border flow? e.g. EU user query, async features, embeddings stored in US - does that happen?
[06:51] Marco: Example: If you allow multi-region fallback and have embedding storage in the US, then embeddings could be stored in the US. For strict EU-only, you'd set region pinning and ensure embedding storage is provisioned in EU. We'll include the mapping in the subprocessor spreadsheet.
[07:10] Elena: What about the managed metadata that Redwood uses for routing and billing — does it contain customer content?
[07:18] Marco: Billing metadata contains usage counters and token counts, not raw content. For customers who request it, we can provide privacy-preserving aggregates and disable some telemetry.
[07:30] Tom: On SLA: If we require strict EU pinning and capacity is exceeded, what's the fallback negotiation?
[07:36] Jenna: We can offer reserved Dedicated capacity in EU to avoid fallback. That's part of the Dedicated offering. There's a cost/throughput tradeoff. We'll include a cost example.
[07:48] Elena: Any customer references in regulated industries using your private deployment with in-region KMS?
[07:54] Jenna: We can share redacted references and a case study of a healthcare customer who deployed private with BYOK. We'll send that.
[08:04] Priya: Ok let's talk timelines - procurement and legal will need the subprocessor list and contracts ASAP. Can you deliver in a week?
[08:12] Jenna: Yes, we'll get subprocessor inventory and SOC 2 by 2026-12-09, KMS doc by 12-13, and propose 12-15 for the technical deep dive.
[08:20] Elena: We'll prepare our compliance checklist and share before the deep dive.
[08:24] (Background cross-talk)
[08:32] Marco: Quick note on implementation: for BYOK you will need to create a key in your cloud KMS, grant the Redwood runtime unwrap permission scoped to the service account, and optionally use a custom IAM role. Our sample Terraform does that. We'll also provide an option for HSM-backed keys in the cloud provider.
[09:00] Tom: Does Redwood ever hold plaintext data in storage? e.g. embeddings or logs?
[09:07] Marco: No plaintext sensitive content is stored at rest; content is encrypted with data keys. Embeddings are stored encrypted. We keep encryption metadata but not plaintext.
[09:20] Elena: Do you have intrusion detection, and do you push alerts to our SIEM?
[09:26] Marco: We can stream security events to your SIEM via a secure syslog or webhook. We also support S3 export of alerts with signed delivery.
[09:38] Priya: For the architecture deep dive on 12-15, who should attend from Redwood?
[09:44] Jenna: Marco (SE) will lead, and we'll bring our infra eng and product security folks. We'll send a calendar invite.

[09:55] Closing recap by Jenna: Action items - we'll send SOC2, subprocessor list, KMS guide, sample VPC/Terraform, and schedule the 12-15 session.
[10:05] Elena: Thanks. If you can also call out any subprocessors outside the EU for the escrow decision that would help procurement.
[10:12] Jenna: Yes will do.

(End of transcript - recorded 58 minutes; truncated transcript shows main highlights and Q/A.)
